1. Scientific Analysis

Analysis Type

Deterministic lattice metrology (FFT Bragg geometry via measure_lattice_constant) plus film/substrate discrimination (fourier_reflection_map satellite census + raw per-row/column intensity profiling).

Interpretation

The FFT-based metrology returns a square, essentially cubic projected cell: a1 = 0.403 nm, a2 = 0.4005 nm, gamma = 90.0 deg (lattice_constant 0.4017 ± 0.0077 nm). This is the perovskite ABO3 pseudocubic {100} spacing and matches both the LSAT substrate (a ≈ 0.3868 nm) and the LLTO film (pseudocubic a ≈ 0.386–0.39 nm) to within the ~3–4% calibration uncertainty expected for a single-frame FOV-derived pixel size — i.e., the measured ~0.40 nm is consistent with a perovskite lattice viewed down a <100> zone axis, with the absolute value biased slightly high by calibration. The reciprocal lattice is internally self-consistent: the (1,0)/(0,1) fundamentals at 0.4015 nm, their {110} at 0.284 nm, and {200} at 0.2008 nm form a clean centered-square census with explained_fraction = 0.86 and 44 indexed reflections, single-lattice (multi_lattice = false). The reported nn_distance of 0.2842 nm is NOT a lattice constant — it is the bright-column-to-bright-column {110} projected spacing (= a/sqrt2), because a {110}-type reflection is resolved (centered_sublattice = true). The lattice constant proper is the ~0.401 nm fundamental; these two quantities must be kept distinct. Critically, the 'strongest satellite' at 0.4015 nm flagged as a candidate is a spacing-relation artifact, not a physical superstructure: 0.4015 nm IS the fundamental {100} spacing, and the tool only labeled it a 'satellite' because it is 2x the 0.2008 nm {200} reflection — the {200} is the harmonic of {100}, not the other way around. The superstructure discriminator confirms this reading: spot_snr_domain (55.9) is only marginally above bulk (48.0), superstructure_domain_fraction = 0.0, and the verdict is explicitly 'NOT confirmed as a localized ordered domain (ambiguous / possible edge artifact).' There is therefore no evidence for a resolved vacancy-ordered or cation-ordered superlattice domain in this frame — consistent with, but not proof of, a disordered (non-superstructured) LLTO/substrate region within the field of view. The row-intensity profile shows a strong smooth ramp/step in the lower band (step_amplitude ~2935, ramp_span ~3212), correctly attributed to shading / thickness gradient rather than a per-column Z-contrast interface step; the column profile shows no clear step (step_amplitude ~270, within shading/noise). The bright bottom band is a specimen-thickness/shading gradient and should not be read as the film/substrate interface.

3. Scientific Claims

Claim 1: The imaged region is a single perovskite lattice with square projected cell a1 = 0.403 nm, a2 = 0.4005 nm, gamma = 90.0 deg (pseudocubic {100} ≈ 0.401 nm; {110} bright-column NN = 0.284 nm), consistent with a <100>-zone perovskite (LLTO film / LSAT substrate) within calibration uncertainty, with no confirmed superstructure (spot_snr_domain 55.9 vs bulk 48.0, domain_fraction 0.0).

Scientific Impact: Establishes the projected crystallography and confirms coherent perovskite stacking with no resolvable cation/vacancy-ordered superlattice domain in this field, setting the baseline needed to detect ordering or strain elsewhere in the LLTO/LSAT system.

Literature Search Query: Has anyone observed a single-phase, non-superstructured pseudocubic perovskite lattice (a ≈ 0.40 nm, {110} spacing 0.284 nm) in LLTO thin films on LSAT viewed down a <100> zone axis?

Keywords: LLTO, LSAT, perovskite, lattice constant, HAADF STEM, superstructure

4. Caveats & Limitations

Absolute lattice value (~0.401 nm) carries ~3-4% calibration uncertainty from the FOV-derived pixel size and reads high versus bulk LLTO/LSAT (~0.386-0.39 nm); the ratio a2/a1 ≈ 0.994 and 90 deg geometry are the reliable, calibration-independent quantities. The 0.4015 nm 'satellite' is a harmonic-relation artifact (it is the fundamental, with {200} as its harmonic), NOT a real superstructure reflection. The superstructure verdict is 'ambiguous / possible edge artifact' — the satellite present in the PSD is not a confirmed localized ordered domain, and its origin cannot be settled from this single frame. The prominent bright bottom band is a shading/thickness ramp, not a film/substrate interface, so no film-vs-substrate lattice discrimination can actually be made from this frame. NN (0.2842 nm) is a column-spacing, not a lattice translation.
